// exp.ts — ONE EXPORT SITE PER SPECIFIER KIND, and per ERASURE MARKER.
//
// A SEPARATE FILE rather than more lines in a.ts, for the reason
// era-position.js exists in the era corpus: a.ts is asserted site for site
// against node's own resolver, and every assertion in that comparison is keyed
// on `(file, line, specifier)`. An export form that carries a source would move
// the line numbers of ten import sites; one that does not carries no specifier
// at all and would read as a site the oracle never enumerated.
//
// IT IMPORTS NOTHING, deliberately. `import_site` is `import_declaration` plus
// `import_expression` and this file contains neither, so the census, the
// oracle comparison and every shape count in test/js-modules.test.ts see
// exactly what they saw before it existed. What it adds is EXPORT bindings,
// which is a different relation.

const internal = 1;
const alsoInternal = 2;
const shorthand = 3;

// THE RENAME. The external name is not the internal one, so a rule reading
// `local` and a rule reading `exported` derive different rows and a mutant that
// swaps them is observable. Every other export form in this repository has the
// two names equal.
export { internal as external };

// ...AND THE SHORTHAND, where they ARE equal. It is here as the control: with
// only the rename above, a rule that read `exported` for both columns would
// still produce one row per specifier and only the pair would be wrong.
export { shorthand };

// THE TWO ERASURE MARKERS, which are the same two an import carries and
// neither implies the other — measured against babel 8 rather than recalled:
//
//   export type { X }   -> ExportNamedDeclaration exportKind "type",
//                          and its ExportSpecifier exportKind "VALUE"
//   export { type X }   -> ExportNamedDeclaration exportKind "value",
//                          and its ExportSpecifier exportKind "type"
//
// So reading either marker alone gets one of the two forms wrong, and the
// specifier of a type-only declaration says the OPPOSITE of the truth.
type Erased = { tag: 'Erased' };
type AlsoErased = { tag: 'AlsoErased' };

export type { Erased as ErasedOut };
export { type AlsoErased as AlsoErasedOut, alsoInternal as alsoExternal };

// THE NAMESPACE RE-EXPORT, ES2020. babel parses `export * as ns from` as an
// ExportNamedDeclaration whose one specifier is an ExportNamespaceSpecifier —
// NOT an ExportAllDeclaration — and that specifier carries an `exported` child
// and NO `local` child. There is no local name for `* as ns` at all, which is
// why the modules layer binds it to `"*"`, exactly as an ImportNamespace-
// Specifier's imported name is `"*"`.
export * as everything from './b.ts';

// ...and the plain `export * from`, which has NO specifier node of any kind.
// It is here so that "a declaration with no specifiers" is a case the export
// binding rules meet rather than a case they were never shown.
export * from './types2.ts';
